museum: Phoebe A. Hearst Museum of Anthropology
museum_original_name: Phoebe A. Hearst Museum of Anthropology, University of California, Berkeley
stated_count_source: '19 crocodile mummies and mummy parts' - UC Berkeley News, Anne Brice, 2 March 2021 https://news.berkeley.edu/2021/03/02/crocodile-mummies/
possible_additional_holdings: Portal also lists 6-20930 'Papyrus fragment' = 'Crocodile eyes of papyrus. Ptolemaic.' (10 pieces, Cemetery 5, Tebtunis) and 6-20959 'Crocodile figure' (gesso/plaster/paint, 'form is stuffed with linen and papyrus, mounted on wooden slab', Cemetery 5 Tebtunis) - possibly crocodile-mummy decoration / pseudo-mummy, not recorded as objects; 6-20315 limestone Sobek statuette 'from Crocodile mummy' (statue, excluded). Grenfell & Hunt found hundreds of crocodile mummies at Tebtunis 1899-1900; most were broken for papyri.
image_license: UNKNOWN (not stated in record JSON; images served from webapps.cspace.berkeley.edu/pahma/imageserver)
api_url: https://portal.hearstmuseum.berkeley.edu/catalog.json?q=<term> (Blacklight JSON; HTML pages behind AWS WAF challenge, JSON reachable with browser User-Agent)
notes: 22 DB records recorded (incl. 4 pseudo-/possibly fake items in lot 6-21629a-d, 2 likely duplicate legacy records 5-21629c/5-21635, 1 decoration record 6-20100.2), consistent with the official figure of 19 mummies and mummy parts. Tebtunis material (Grenfell & Hunt 1899-1900, Hearst funding) in Dept Ancient Egypt; 5-512/5-513/5-514 lot (Acc.6, 1899, Phoebe Hearst) catalogued under Africa dept. Parts of 5-514 were sent to Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County (L.1186-701a,b; L.1186-702). Several items loaned to Bancroft Library (Object Lessons exhibit 2019-2021).

possible_additional_holdings: Press release 'Inside Ancient Egypt': 'On display are 31 animal mummies including cats, falcons, even a crocodile' (may be same or different from the neonatal crocodile in the Mummies exhibition); news on 2015 NHM LA venue of the Field Museum's 'Mummies' exhibition mentions baby crocodiles and 'a crocodile mummy encased in an intricate, segmented linen-and-canvas shroud' (secondary).
notes: Anthropology collections database (EMu web) blocked by Cloudflare Turnstile/BunkerWeb for curl and WebFetch; inventory numbers could not be retrieved - needs manual browser check (search 'crocodile' in Egypt). Count of crocodile mummies unknown (at least 1).
